messages.body_plain:
Hello,

Thanks a lot for this wonderful package. I have been testing it for a while now and had some questions- apologies for how long this is.

My first question is about normalisation:

My experiment is a pulldown based experiment, where I don’t expect most proteins to be similar across conditions. My issue is I am not sure how to assess if this normalisation makes sense ? (or even if my assumption is true and if i should then just use median normalisation). My other question is about batch effects:

I have a rather large LFQ design, where I have 4 conditions (Lamp1, Lamp2, Nes, UT) each with 4 biological replicates and each of those with 4 technical replicates. One tech replicate per biological rep (rep1) was ran on the same day for all the conditions. The other three were ran a few weeks later one after the other for all conditions. Because of this weird loading, I can see there’s a batch effect, so all the tech reps ran one after the other correlated more to each other than to the one ran on a separate day.

At this point, I am not sure if I should ignore the repeat tech replicates and just run my analysis using the first technical rep- I am worried perhaps some peptides were lost after storage for weeks?  but also this is a lot of data to discard so i am not sure if there’s a way to account for this batch effect in MsStats?

Thank you!

messages.subject: Re: normalisation and batch effect
messages.body_plain:
Hi Reem,

For the first question regarding normalization with standards: if you have multiple standards, I suggest that you use only a subset of the standards for the normalization, and then see how the normalization affected the remaining standards. If the variation in the left-out standards improved, this means that the normalization worked. If after the normalization the left-out standards remained the same or became more noisy, this means that the normalization failed. Typically normalization fails because it makes unrealistic assumptions (see below).

For the question regarding batch effects: global normalization based on standards assumes that the experimental artifact that affected the standards affected the rest of the proteins in exactly the same way. If this is true, you would not have a pronounced batch effect after a standards-based normalization. If you still see a batch effect after a standards-based normalization, it is possible that (a) the global standards-based normalization made wrong assumptions, or (b) the artifacts are protein-specific and are not captured by the standards. In (b), it is possible to introduce batch as another condition in MSstats. You'd annotate the runs as if they came from 8 conditions: Lamp1.batch1, Lamp2.batch1, Nes.batch1, UT.batch1, Lamp1.batch2, Lamp2.batch2, Nes.batch2, UT.batch2, and then create contrasts that compare two conditions on average over the two batches. E.g., in the order above, comparing Nes vs UT would be a contrast 0, 0, 0.5, -0.5, 0, 0, 0.5, -0.5. This approach will reduce the degrees of freedom of the error but can still gain sensitivity if there is a substantial batch effect

Hope this helps at least somewhat. Thank you for using MSstats

Sincerely
Olga

messages.body_plain:
Hi Luiz,

1) You are exactly correct that MSstats multiplies the coefficients by the values in the contrast matrix. What this means when you use fractions is that MSstats will average over those coefficients.

Hello,

I dug into this problem and was able to build the annotation file given the MaxQ evidence file. I think your problem was the Run name in your annotation did not match the full MaxQ run name. The code below creates the annotation file that works for me.

```
library(tidyverse)

substrRight <- function(x, n){
    substr(x, nchar(x)-n+1, nchar(x))
}

annot = evidence %>% distinct(`Raw file`, Experiment)
annot$BioReplicate = unlist(lapply(annot$Experiment, function(x){substrRight(x,2)}))
annot = annot %>% mutate(BioReplicate = str_replace(BioReplicate, "E", ""))
annot$BioReplicate = as.integer(annot$BioReplicate)

annot$Condition = substr(annot$Experiment,1,nchar(annot$Experiment)-3)
```

Hope this helps!

Devon
